findings.location: <article> paragraph 3 (source: "man and beast battle its ferocity")
findings.source_quote: "Man and beast battle its ferocity, and even the lifeless machinery rebels against winter’s adamant arrival."
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the sense correctly into Kiswahili. Replace the incorrect word "mizoga" (carcasses) with an appropriate word for animals/beasts. For example: "Mwanadamu na wanyama wanapigana na ukali wake, hata mashine zisizo na uhai zinapinga kuingia kwa msimu wa baridi." Preserve sentence structure and HTML tags.
findings.translation_quote: "Mwanadamu na mizoga huzitaka nguvu zake, na hata mashine zisizo na maisha zinopinga kuingia kwa msimu huyu mkali."

findings.source_quote: "Chilly drafts penetrate every crack and crevice, forcing their heartless presence into the most private chambers."
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the unclear/incorrect word "punku" with a standard Kiswahili equivalent such as "mchezo" is wrong; use "pengo" or "nyufa". Suggested sentence: "Upepo baridi hupenya katika kila pengo na nyufa, ikiingiza uwepo wake usio na huruma hata katika vyumba vya kibinafsi zaidi."
findings.translation_quote: "Upepo baridi hupenya katika kila mwanya na punku, kuingiza uwepo wake usio na huruma katika vyumba vya kibinafsi zaidi."

findings.source_quote: "The bounties of harvest provide an aura of rejoicing in their sheaves..."
findings.suggested_fix: Avoid leaving the English loanword capitalized as "Bounty" and translate it into Kiswahili. Suggested: "Mavuno ya majani huleta furaha katika vimbili vyao..." or simply "Mavuno yanatoa hisia za shangwe..."
findings.translation_quote: "Bounty za mavuno huleta furaha katika mizinga yao, na mioyo ya watu bado inafurahi..."

findings.location: <article> paragraph 18 (source: "a luthier by the name of Stradivari created violins")
findings.source_quote: "In the 1700s, a luthier by the name of Stradivari created violins unequaled in their excellence for beautiful sound."
findings.suggested_fix: Correctly translate technical terms and the object. A "luthier" is a maker of stringed instruments, and "violins" must be translated as "fidla" or the common Kiswahili term "viyolini" (or "fidla/vyolin" depending on style). Also fix the subsequent sentence that refers to "violins" (not tastes). Suggested translation: "Mnamo karne ya 1700, fundi ala wa majembe ambaye aliitwa Stradivari alitengeneza violini visivyolinganishwa kwa uzuri wa sauti." Preserve HTML and surrounding paragraph structure.
findings.translation_quote: "Mnamo karne ya 1700, mchongaji wa vioo aitwaye Stradivari alitengeneza vionjo ambavyo havikulinganishwa kwa urembo wa sauti."

findings.location: <article> paragraph 18 (source: "the wood of the day had been seasoned by difficult winters")
findings.source_quote: "most have resolved that the wood of the day had been seasoned by difficult winters, producing a quality that cannot be replicated in our day."
findings.suggested_fix: If keeping the violin example, ensure 'wood' and 'seasoned' are clear. Translate as: "mbao za wakati huo zilikuwa zimefunikwa/kuoshwa na majira magumu ya baridi, zikitoa ubora usio wezekana kurudiwa katika zama zetu."
findings.translation_quote: "mbao za siku zake zilikuwa zimekaza kwa majira ya baridi magumu, zikatoa ubora usioweza kurudiwa katika wakati wetu."
